title: The Quran: Surah 2, al-Baqarah (The Heifer), verse 255 (Ayat al-Kursi)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 2, versículo 255 (Ayat al-Kursi). O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to the verse, what does not overtake Him?
questions.why: O versículo diz: 'Neither slumber overtakes Him, nor sleep.'

options: to speak on behalf of someone else, asking something for them
questions.why: 'Intercede' é interceder, pedir algo a favor de outra pessoa.

questions.q: The verse asks 'Who is he that can intercede with Him except with His permission?' What answer does the question suggest?
options: No one, unless He allows it
questions.why: A pergunta inclui 'except with His permission', por isso ninguém o pode fazer sem essa permissão.

options: With a name and an exclamation mark

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up the verse?
options: It tells a story about a journey
It describes Him as living and never sleeping, as owner of all things, and as one whose care for the heavens and the earth does not burden Him
questions.why: O versículo diz 'the Living', 'neither slumber... nor sleep', 'To Him belongs everything' e 'does not burden Him'.

B2.discussion: The verse describes with negatives ('neither slumber... nor sleep', 'does not burden Him'). Why might a text describe something by saying what it is not?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Explain in your own words what the verse says about Him.

questions.why: O versículo diz: 'His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth'.

questions.q: In 'they cannot grasp any of His knowledge, except as He wills', 'grasp' is closest to:
'He knows what is before them, and what is behind them.' What does this pair suggest?
options: That He knows only the past
That He knows only the future
That His knowledge is complete, covering what is in front and what is behind

questions.q: The verse uses pairs: 'slumber... sleep', 'before them... behind them', 'the heavens and the earth'. What effect do the pairs have?
options: They change the topic each time
They give a sense of completeness, covering both sides of each idea
questions.why: Cada par cobre os dois lados de uma ideia.

options: The verse combines statements about who He is, what He does not need, what belongs to Him, what He knows, and the limits of what others can do
The verse is only a list of names
The verse tells a story with characters
The verse gives instructions for travel
questions.why: O versículo passa por vários aspectos: quem Ele é, o sono, a posse, o conhecimento e os limites dos outros.

C1.discussion: The verse is a series of short statements, each adding a new aspect. How does the accumulation shape the way the reader pictures the whole?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how the pairs of words in the verse contribute to its meaning.

questions.q: Which two titles close the verse?
questions.why: O versículo acaba com 'He is the Most High, the Great.'

questions.q: 'Neither slumber overtakes Him, nor sleep' inverts ordinary word order. What effect does this have?
questions.why: A estrutura 'neither... nor' e a ordem invertida dão um tom solene.

questions.q: The verse moves between statements about Him and statements about what others cannot do (intercede, grasp). What does this contrast suggest?
options: That everything else is equal to Him
A contrast between His completeness and the limits of everything else
That the verse is about travel
questions.why: A pergunta sobre interceder e 'they cannot grasp' marcam o que os outros não podem fazer.

questions.q: Which description of the verse's structure is best supported?
options: An opening name and two titles, a statement about sleep, a statement of ownership, a question, statements about knowledge and the Throne, and two closing titles
questions.why: O versículo segue essa sequência, do nome inicial aos dois títulos finais.

questions.q: The verse opens with titles ('the Living, the Everlasting') and closes with titles ('the Most High, the Great'). What does this framing do?
options: It gives the verse a frame of titles around the statements in between
It turns the verse into a question
questions.why: Os títulos no início e no fim fecham os restantes elementos entre eles.

C2.discussion: The verse has a frame of titles at the start and the end, with statements about sleep, ownership, intercession and knowledge between. How does the frame hold together such different statements?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the verse is built, referring to specific words and to the pattern of statements, pairs and titles.
